purpose: Prioritize IRFEN research and validation effort according to climate-regime plausibility, historical activation behavior, episodic response, demographic exposure and critical-connectivity consequences without converting research priority into operational risk or alerts.

research_dimensions.meaning: Qualitative compatibility of the candidate mechanism with the current/target climate regime. Must be source-supported and scenario-dated.
Strength and recurrence of verified activation/impact evidence across comparable historical regimes.
Evidence that an arid or normally dry catchment can respond strongly to isolated intense episodes.
Direct population exposure; never used alone to rank physical activation.
Potential to cut highways, bridges, water systems, irrigation, schools, health access or isolate settlements.
Availability of official geometry, event outcomes, observations and reproducible sources.
Unresolved uncertainty. High uncertainty does not mean low hazard and may justify targeted research.

historical_regime_windows_to_reconstruct.label: 1982-1983 strong El Nino
historical_regime_windows_to_reconstruct.role: historical climate-regime comparison; verify local event evidence before assigning candidate behavior

historical_regime_windows_to_reconstruct.label: 1997-1998 strong El Nino
historical_regime_windows_to_reconstruct.role: historical climate-regime comparison; verify local event evidence before assigning candidate behavior

historical_regime_windows_to_reconstruct.label: 2017 coastal El Nino
historical_regime_windows_to_reconstruct.role: high-value recent historical comparison for north/central coast and selected south-coast episodic responses

historical_regime_windows_to_reconstruct.label: 2023 coastal warm event
historical_regime_windows_to_reconstruct.role: recent comparison for basin-specific activation and non-activation evidence

historical_regime_windows_to_reconstruct.label: 2024-2026 recent local extremes
historical_regime_windows_to_reconstruct.role: recent episodic-response evidence, especially for Ica-Nazca, coastal Arequipa and Moquegua-Ilo

impact_balance_policy.principle: Physical activation potential and consequence are evaluated separately, then combined only for research prioritization.
examples_of_critical_consequences: Panamericana or other strategic road interruption

scenario_corridors.rationale: Warm coastal/central Pacific regimes can strongly increase rainfall and flood/debris-flow opportunity over north and central Pacific-facing basins, subject to event-specific verification.
discovery_gaps: Pativilca and Fortaleza/Paramonga: hydrologic separation plus El Nino event reconstruction
Huarmey-Culebras: split official hydrologic systems and normalize 2017 evidence
Casma-Sechin-Yautan/Grande: child-unit decomposition and event/observation packages
Chimbote-Lacramarca-lower Santa: territorial exposure with separate hydrologic children
Viru: basin geometry, event ledger and observations
Chao: Huamanzaña, Chorobal and local pluvial drainage kept separate
Moche: river flooding separated from Trujillo-area debris-flow ravines
Chicama: basin/tributary normalization using the existing hydraulic study and recurrent critical-point evidence
Jequetepeque: basin/tributary identity, El Nino event reconstruction, regulated-system observations and lower-valley exposure
Chepén: resolve Chamán, La Morana and Avispero while keeping Jequetepeque separate
Máncora-Los Órganos: normalize quebrada Fernández, 2026 activation and unresolved local Los Órganos catchments
Zorritos-Bocapán: decompose multiple short-response coastal ravines with 2017/Yaku evidence
Río Tumbes: exploit observed 2023 inundation layers and Cabo Inga/El Tigre hydrometric observations

scenario_corridors.rationale: Arid south-coast catchments can produce high-impact episodic debris flows or floods even when seasonal rainfall background is not broadly wet; recent activation and connectivity consequences justify a separate high-priority lane.

focus: ravines crossing Costanera and access roads

discovery_gaps: Moquegua-Ilo/Osmore: exact official basin geometry and local Ilo/Pacocha ravine identity for the Aug-2026 outcomes
Torata-Chacane: exact channel/catchment, parent hydrographic unit and receiving-channel topology
Locumba-Mirave: resolve Mirave source catchment and freeze a primary official 2015 event source before using 2015
Sama-Quebrada de los Burros: resolve whether the named event location corresponds to a reproducible hydrologic child
Caplina-Uchusuma-Pachia: keep Caplina and Uchusuma geometries separate and resolve the 2019 Pachia huaico source catchment
Tacna Intercuenca 13155: separate future discovery unit before any local event attribution

required_before_high_priority_deep_dive: named hydrologic/geodynamic unit or reproducible discovery geometry
at least one official or otherwise admissible event/outcome source OR explicit UNKNOWN if studying physical susceptibility only
required_before_research_closeout: verified positive or independently adjudicated control evidence
all production and alerting guards fail closed

triggers: new official activation or impact report
new verified geometry or exposure evidence
new infrastructure or road/bridge vulnerability evidence
new observed non-impact control with adequate hydrometeorology
dynamic_reprioritization.rule: A scenario update may raise or lower research effort, but cannot itself activate a zone, classify an event, create a negative control, or change an operational threshold.
